clauses.scope_note: Section 7.1(a): applies to a Recipient’s use of the Discloser’s Confidential Information; Confidential Information includes Customer Content. Section 7.2 exceptions apply where the information is public through no fault of Recipient, was previously possessed or known, was rightfully disclosed without restriction by a third party, or was independently developed without use of the Confidential Information.
clauses.condition_explanation: use_only_to_exercise_agreement_rights_or_fulfill_agreement_obligations means the Recipient uses the Discloser’s Confidential Information only for those purposes, subject to the Section 7.2 exceptions.

clauses.scope_note: Sections 7.1(c) and 7.3: applies to disclosure of the Discloser’s Confidential Information. Disclosure is permitted to Affiliates, employees, contractors, and agents with a need to know who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as restrictive; disclosure required by law is permitted subject to reasonable efforts to notify the Discloser beforehand to the extent permitted.
clauses.condition_explanation: not_permitted_disclosure is false for a disclosure to a qualifying need-to-know recipient bound by the required confidentiality obligations, or a disclosure required by law for which reasonable prior notice efforts are made to the extent permitted; otherwise it is true.

obligation_items.content: Do not disclose the Discloser’s Confidential Information except as expressly permitted by the Agreement.
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever the Recipient would disclose the information, except for a permitted disclosure under Section 7.3.

clauses.scope_note: Section 7.1(b): applies to the Recipient’s handling of the Discloser’s Confidential Information, subject to the Section 7.2 exceptions.
clauses.condition_explanation: reasonable_protection_measures_taken means the Recipient takes reasonable measures to protect the Confidential Information.

obligation_items.content: Take reasonable measures to protect the Discloser’s Confidential Information.
obligation_items.trigger: While the Recipient holds or handles the Confidential Information, except to the extent the Section 7.2 exceptions apply.

clauses.scope_note: Sections 9.1–9.2: Customer grants OpenAI only the limited rights reasonably necessary to deliver the Services; that permission extends to subcontractors or subprocessors. The Agreement otherwise grants OpenAI no IP Rights in Customer Content except as expressly set forth.
clauses.condition_explanation: reasonably_necessary_to_deliver_services means the use is reasonably necessary for OpenAI to deliver the Services.

clauses.scope_note: Section 9.3: if Customer provides Feedback regarding the Services, Customer grants OpenAI the right to use and exploit that Feedback without restriction or compensation.
clauses.condition_explanation: customer_provides_feedback means Customer has provided Feedback regarding the Services.

clauses.scope_note: Section 10: absent express prior written permission in each instance, neither Party may include the other Party’s name or logo on websites, media, or marketing materials, or make a public statement about its relationship with the other Party or the Agreement.
clauses.condition_explanation: not_express_prior_written_permission_for_this_instance means the acting Party lacks express prior written permission for the particular use or statement.

obligation_items.content: Do not include the other Party’s name or logo on websites, media, or marketing materials, and do not make a public statement about the relationship or Agreement, without express prior written permission in each instance.
obligation_items.object: The other Party’s name or logo, or a public statement about the relationship or Agreement
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever the Party would make the specified use or statement, unless it has express prior written permission for that instance.

coverage_notes: The Security Measures, Audit Reports, DPA, Healthcare Addendum, Service Credit Terms, Order Form, Pricing Page, and OpenAI Policies are incorporated or referenced but not supplied here; their substantive terms are not inferred.

Several operative provisions cannot be faithfully represented with the supplied activity/object schema: OpenAI’s security-measure and audit-report delivery duties; the incorporated DPA obligations; the PHI-specific prohibition; payment, tax, invoice-dispute, and billing-information duties; suspension and account-control provisions; and the requirement that a Recipient be responsible for certain personnel breaches. Related target paragraphs are marked UNRESOLVED where applicable.
Section 9.1’s reservation that Customer receives no ownership rights in the Services is noted in scope, but the schema does not provide an ownership-rights activity.

paragraph_audit.reason: The paragraph contains operative OpenAI duties to comply with and provide Audit Reports under specified conditions, a Customer termination option with a five-business-day deadline, a conditional PHI prohibition, and duties under the incorporated DPA. These cannot all be faithfully represented with the permitted activities and objects, and the DPA and referenced security terms are absent.

The paragraph imposes operative payment, billing-information, tax, invoice-dispute, and payment-uplift duties and provides fee-charging and suspension terms. The supplied Charge activity is defined for charges to third parties, not payments to the provider, so these duties cannot be faithfully encoded as licensee actions.

Sections 7.1–7.3 are represented with the agreement-purpose restriction, disclosure restriction and exceptions, and reasonable-protection duty. Section 7.2’s specified exceptions and Section 7.3’s permitted disclosure paths are stated in scope and conditions.

The paragraph grants OpenAI discretion to request or directly suspend or terminate an End User account and to limit or suspend Services, and imposes notice, tailoring, and restoration-cooperation duties. Those actions and duties are not faithfully representable with the available activities; suspension is not itself a listed activity.

Sections 9.2 and 9.3 are modeled, but Section 9.1 also contains an operative reservation of rights and a limited Customer right to use Services, neither of which is fully expressible as an activity constraint in the supplied schema.
The prohibition on specified publicity and public statements, including its express-prior-written-permission exception for each instance, is represented.
